title: Sticky-key affinity pools for KV cache to reduce fragmentation under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight "sticky-key" affinity layer that groups frequently co-accessed KV entries into short-lived affinity pools tied to batching windows. The goal is to reduce internal fragmentation and long-tail slot churn caused by variable-length contexts and continuous batching without a heavy global compaction pass.
background: We observe two sources of inefficient GPU memory utilization: (1) continuous batching creates many short-lived mixed-size KV allocations which scatter across pools, and (2) runtime eviction heuristics produce slot churn when hot prefixes and cold prefixes interleave. Previous approaches focused on aggressive global compaction or large reserved slabs which increases latency or wastes capacity. We need a low-overhead strategy that improves placement locality and reduces defrag pressure for production workloads with high churn and mixed prompt lengths.
technical_approach:
1) Affinity pools: allocate ephemeral micro-pools (configurable N=4..16) per worker that preferentially accept KV entries tagged with a per-request affinity token (hash of request prefix + model shard id).
2) Sticky-key binding: when a prefix key is first populated in a pooling window, pin subsequent accesses from same affinity token to the same pool for a TTL tied to batching window and token decay.
3) Pool sizing: pools sized dynamically by exponential smoothing of recent allocations; enforce soft headroom to avoid immediate spillover.
4) Remap throttle: background remap actor moves small hot groups instead of large sweeping compaction; remaps are rate-limited by GPU utilization and do not block serving.
5) Eviction hints: encode a 4-bit affinity id in metadata so eviction tries to free space within least-recently-used pools before cross-pool eviction.
6) Integration with continuous batching: attach affinity token to batch routing so multi-request batches with shared prefix affinity get colocated where possible.
7) Fallback: if affinity pools are exhausted, fall back to normal allocation path to maintain correctness.
8) Telemetry: emit pool occupancy histograms, remap bandwidth, affinity hit rate, and fragmentation delta per epoch.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement affinity pools behind a runtime flag for a single low-traffic region and monitor telemetry for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (gradual): enable for 10% of workers across regions with remap throttle conservative. Phase 3 (widen): increase to 50% with tuning of pool sizing. Phase 4 (global): enable by default and remove flag after 4-6 cycles if metrics stable. Each phase has abort flag and automatic rollback if GPU OOMs or latency regression > 3p.
telemetry: Emit new metrics: affinity_pool_count, affinity_pool_occupancy_bucketed, affinity_hit_rate, remap_ops_per_minute, remap_bytes_moved, pool_eviction_attempts, fragmentation_estimate_bytes. Surface these in console under per-model memory panel and add alert if remap_bytes_moved spikes > baseline * 4 or affinity_hit_rate < 0.2.
acceptance_criteria: Affinity pools implemented behind feature flag and controlled via runtime config
No increase in 99th percentile token latency greater than 5% in canary region
Affinity hit rate >= 0.45 on mixed-length production prompt traces in canary
Observed reduction in fragmentation estimate (bytes of non-contiguous free space) >= 20% after 2 weeks in canary
No unexplained GPU OOMs attributable to remap operations during canary
